reuse.why: The new handler and existing consumers reuse the recurrence converter and weekend adjustment helpers, although schedule construction and occurrence mapping remain repeated.

duplication.why: The range handler repeats the upcoming handler's enumeration pipeline, and holiday interpretation is separately encoded through exclusion-date expansion and date membership checks.

placement.why: Recurrence policy remains in shared/schedules.ts, transport handling stays in the schedules server module, and configuration fields live in the existing model.

scope.why: The changes are confined to the requested recurrence features, their consumers, tests, and release notes.

maintainability.why: Shared helpers provide a reasonable foundation, but duplicated orchestration, arbitrary 14-day and 100-year horizons, and an untyped new configuration helper increase maintenance burden.

bypasses_abstraction.where: The new range handler calls recurConfigToRSchedule, recurConfigToExdates, and applyWeekendRule rather than independently implementing recurrence adjustment.

disguised_duplication.where: shared/schedules.ts interprets full-date and annual holidays both through materialized exclusion dates in recurConfigToExdates and through string membership in getDateWithSkippedWeekend.

abstraction_drift.where: applyWeekendRule and getDateWithSkippedWeekend each gain a holidays parameter, and recurConfigToRSchedule gains a daily-only skipWeekend branch; consumers continue calling the shared helpers.
